payload.as_is: Pain 1 - the drawn machine is decoration. The systematic machine exists as a compiled canvas, but the interim executor walks one linear token; parallel branches (log_risks beside the M1 spine, candidates/spikes/build chunks as sub-machines) cannot activate together. Witness: today's session - the board renders the machine as one column, and the i2-era iterations all ran the four-step lean sequence. Pain 2 - calls block on long work. A submit that lands on an engine-filled verify state holds the call for the full suite. Witness: the call log, 840 calls - se_loop_submit p90 at 4.8s against a 4ms median; the owner flagged it unprompted. Pain 3 - the working laws are prose. Update discipline, gate parking with a watcher, project-at-boot, commit timing: each was violated at least once TODAY by a fresh session following the contract text. Witness: this morning's boot skipped the project question; three commits landed mid-state; the toll went 679 minutes without an update overnight. Pain 4 - the retro leans on ad-hoc scripts and direct reads. The inbox and the call log have no served lane; aggregation was a hand-written python one-off, twice rewritten. Witness: the two logged se_help misses at 07:49 and the aggregation script's wrong-keys retry in this session. Pain 5 - engine edits need owner ritual. Every MCP-server change waits for /mcp reconnect se; the board needs hand-run netstat/taskkill cycles. Witness: two board cycles today; the reconnect chore noted 2026-07-23 with the Vite-HMR lead. Pain 6 - the process record cannot answer its own questions. Failure lines log no clause and dispatches double-log, so the retro's clause ranking was impossible from the data. Witness: today's mining - 74 failures, every clause field empty; 28 se_help lines for 14 calls.
